autoMode.//note: Generated from session-log analysis and nine rounds of `claude auto-mode critique`. v18: directional cross-references ('below', 'above') replaced with named references, since section rendering order is not guaranteed; [Credential Leakage] renamed to avoid colliding with the default rule of that name; conditions the classifier cannot verify (gitignored destination, 'synthetic or redacted') replaced with observable ones; registry-override detection extended to environment variables; branch deletion and --mirror split out of [Force Push]; [Off Region Resource] scoped to commands where the region is explicit.
environment: $defaults

Organization: work spans four identities, each with its OWN GitHub account — they are not different orgs under one login, and operating in one requires being authenticated as that identity. PERSONAL: TheVoskamps, github.com (GitHub Team). FABLEGATE: Fablegate, github.com (GitHub Team) — the bulk of current employer work. TELUS: TELUS-Connected-Home, GitHub Enterprise without EMU and without data-residency guarantees, therefore hosted on github.com. STATIONWORKS: orgs Corporate, Infrastructure and Mobilize on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with EMU and US data residency, at sttnwrks.ghe.com; currently low activity. Every repository outside the PUBLIC repository list in the Repository visibility entry holds company-confidential intellectual property belonging to exactly one identity.

Source control: two hosts, four identities, separate GitHub accounts. github.com carries three identities that must not be conflated — TheVoskamps/* (personal), Fablegate/* and TELUS-Connected-Home/*; on that host the ORG name identifies the owner, and the host alone does not. sttnwrks.ghe.com carries StationWorks only, orgs Corporate/*, Infrastructure/* and Mobilize/*; there the hostname identifies the owner. Any other *.ghe.com tenant is an unrelated organisation and is external. Because each identity has its own GitHub account, an operation that reaches a second identity's repository normally implies an authentication switch: treat an operation spanning two identities as crossing an employer boundary, not as ordinary multi-repo work.

Repository visibility: PUBLIC — TheVoskamps/claude-plugins-marketplace, TheVoskamps/claude-config, TheVoskamps/macos-setup, TheVoskamps/gh-repo-config, TheVoskamps/claude-code-log (fork of daaain/claude-code-log), TheVoskamps/Claude-Conversation-Exporter (fork of socketteer/Claude-Conversation-Exporter). The upstreams daaain/* and socketteer/* are EXTERNAL: never push targets, never PR base repositories. Everything else is PRIVATE and company-confidential: all Fablegate/*, all TELUS-Connected-Home/*, all Corporate/*, Infrastructure/* and Mobilize/* on sttnwrks.ghe.com, and any TheVoskamps/* repository not on the PUBLIC list.

Branch conventions: main is the integration branch in every repo. All feature work happens on issue-NNN-<slug> branches created from main. In the Fablegate repos, a merge to main triggers AWS CodePipeline, which builds and publishes packages to CodeArtifact.
Ephemeral scratch paths: <repo>/.claude/worktrees/agent-* (git worktrees for agent runs) and <repo>/.claude/tmp/ (scratch output). Both are gitignored, disposable, and reconstructible.

Cloud provider: AWS, via aws-cli with SSO profiles. Accounts in use: FablegateDevOpsAdmin-251424476988, FablegateManagementAdmin-266735799169, FablegateInfrastructureAdmin-895169747393, FablegateCodeArtifactDeveloper. These are administrator-level profiles; assume any AWS write executed under them has full account blast radius. Regions: us-west-2 is the working region and is where resources normally live. us-east-1 is used ONLY for resources that must be there because the service is global or requires that region — Route 53 hosted zones, CloudFront distributions, ACM certificates attached to CloudFront, and global CMKs. A resource of any other kind being created, modified or deleted in us-east-1 is off-pattern.

Internal package registry: AWS CodeArtifact, domain fablegate-artifacts, repositories fablegate-npm, fablegate-npm-releases, fablegate-npm-candidates, in us-west-2. Endpoints are account-scoped and only these are internal: fablegate-artifacts-251424476988, fablegate-artifacts-266735799169 and fablegate-artifacts-895169747393, each as <domain-owner>.d.codeartifact.us-west-2.amazonaws.com. A codeartifact.amazonaws.com hostname under any other account number, or in any other region, is EXTERNAL. This registry is shared across work identities and is not scoped to one employer.
Secrets management: AWS SSM Parameter Store and AWS Secrets Manager. Secret values are read at runtime by application and CI code and are never committed to a repository.
CI/CD deploy targets: AWS CodePipeline. Known pipelines: fablegate-dataplane-library-pipeline-main, fablegate-infra-inception-pipeline. Both publish to CodeArtifact.

Trusted cloud buckets: None. No S3 bucket is trusted to receive data. This entry supersedes any default 'Trusted cloud buckets' entry above; ignore that heuristic. (Buckets matching s3://fablegate-test-* hold only generated test fixtures — see the corresponding allow rule — but they are still not data-flow destinations.)

Trusted internal domains: github.com, claude.ai, claude.com, and the AWS CodeArtifact endpoints above. There is no VPN, internal network, or self-hosted service in this environment; any other host is external.

Sensitive data locations & audiences (extends the default heuristic, does not narrow it): every private repository named above holds company-confidential IP whose audience is that identity alone. StationWorks repositories on sttnwrks.ghe.com additionally carry US data-residency constraints — their contents must not reach infrastructure outside approved US regions, which constrains WHERE data goes and is separate from confidentiality. Fablegate and TELUS-Connected-Home are confidential but carry no residency obligation. Because TELUS-Connected-Home, Fablegate and TheVoskamps all sit on github.com, a bare github.com destination is not sufficient to establish the owner: the org must be identified. The AWS account numbers and SSO profile names listed in the Cloud provider entry are internal and must never appear in a PUBLIC repository. Real Claude Code session transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl are personal data.

Sensitive remote targets: no long-lived servers, databases, Kubernetes clusters or production hosts are expected to be reachable from this machine, so interactive remote sessions, remote exec and port-forwarding have no expected target. If a command does target one — a database, a container-hosted service, a cluster — treat its appearance as unexpected rather than as evidence it must be a local test double, and apply the relevant rule at full force. This entry supersedes the default 'anything named prod' heuristic above; ignore that heuristic. Deploy surfaces are declared under CI/CD deploy targets, not here.

Protected IaC scopes: IAM and SSO roles, policies and permission sets; VPC and networking resources; and anything in the FablegateManagementAdmin-266735799169 account. This entry supersedes the default Protected IaC scopes heuristic above; ignore that heuristic. All four Fablegate AWS accounts are administrator-scoped and should be treated as production-equivalent regardless of the absence of 'prod' in their names.
Container runtime: podman is the default on this machine; docker is used only for registry interactions with docker.io and ghcr.io.

TheVoskamps/claude-plugins-marketplace contains a security tool (plugins/guardrails, hooks/permission-gate) whose test suites use synthetic hostile command strings as test data — fake hostnames, fake credentials, and malformed command payloads — written into fixture files and parser test tables under plugins/guardrails/** and hooks/permission-gate/**. These are inputs to a parser under test. Writing and reading them is routine; executing any of those command strings is not, and must be judged normally.

Shell variables, working-directory changes, and loop variables in Bash commands are resolved to literals by a deterministic PreToolUse analyzer before you see the command. A bare $VAR or unresolved path in a delete or write target should therefore not occur; if one does, the analyzer did not produce it and it should be treated as unverifiable.

Transcript-processing tools: the forks daaain/claude-code-log and socketteer/Claude-Conversation-Exporter parse Claude Code session transcripts. Their test suites contain SYNTHETIC and redacted .jsonl fixtures under test/, tests/, and **/testdata/ inside those checkouts; those are authored test data. Real session transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/ are captured personal data.

Cloud estate: the AWS accounts, SSO profiles, CodeArtifact repositories and CodePipeline pipelines named in these rules are shared across the work identities above and are not scoped to a single employer.
allow: [Notation] <repo> means the root of the git working tree the session started in, not a directory literally named "repo". <id> and agent-<id> mean any single literal directory-name suffix. <other> means any value other than the one under discussion. These are metavariables, not paths to search for.

[Scratch Tmp] Creating, writing to, and removing files and directories under <repo>/.claude/tmp/ is allowed, including recursive removal of a subdirectory THIS session created. That directory is shared scratch space other concurrent sessions also write to: removing a subdirectory this session did not create, or the <repo>/.claude/tmp/ directory itself, is not covered.
[Mkdir] Creating directories with mkdir or mkdir -p anywhere under a repository working tree is allowed.

[Worktree Lifecycle] git worktree add, remove, list and prune is allowed for a single named worktree directory <repo>/.claude/worktrees/agent-<id>, including removing one whose branch has already been pushed. Recursive removal of the <repo>/.claude/worktrees/ parent, or of a worktree this session did not create, is not covered.
[Read Only Git] git fetch, git status, git log, git diff, git show and branch listing against github.com/TheVoskamps or github.com/Fablegate is allowed.

[Feature Branch Push] Pushing an issue-NNN-* feature branch to origin, and opening or updating a pull request from that branch against main in the SAME repository, is allowed for the repositories named in the environment entries. This blesses the destination only: content rules -- Sensitive-Source Provenance, the default Credential Leakage rule, Out-of-Place Publication, Excess Sensitive Detail -- still apply in full, and a push to one of the repositories listed as PUBLIC in the Repository visibility entry is a publication step for any content that is not that repository's own work. Not covered: force-push, pushes to main, and any cross-repository or fork-to-upstream pull request.

[Issue Triage] Updating GitHub issue and PR metadata on the repositories named in the environment entries is allowed: labels, assignees, milestones, Projects V2 item fields, issue open/close state, and PR draft/ready state. This applies through any vehicle -- gh api GraphQL or REST, gh issue/gh pr subcommands, or an MCP GitHub tool. Not covered, and judged normally: submitting or dismissing a PR review, which collides with the Self-Approval rule; merging; and any additional operation bundled into the same GraphQL document alongside a permitted one -- a multi-operation mutation is judged by its broadest operation.

[CodeArtifact Install] Installing dependencies from the fablegate-artifacts CodeArtifact repositories named in the environment entries is allowed, including aws codeartifact get-authorization-token and aws codeartifact login to refresh the registry token, and including agent-chosen packages beyond those in the manifest. A CodeArtifact hostname under an account number other than those named in the environment entries is not this rule. Publishing to those repositories is not covered.

[Secret Read] Reading secrets is allowed against the accounts named in the environment entries: aws ssm get-parameter, get-parameters, get-parameters-by-path (including --with-decryption), and aws secretsmanager get-secret-value. This covers RETRIEVAL ONLY, and clears Credential Exploration for these calls. It does not clear Credential Materialization: the value must not appear in a subsequent command line, be echoed to stdout, be written into any file inside a repository working tree, or be sent to any network destination. Judge the retrieval by the command; judge what happens to the value by the command that consumes it.
[Pipeline Read] Read-only AWS CodePipeline inspection is allowed: list-pipelines, list-pipeline-executions, get-pipeline-state, get-pipeline-execution, list-action-executions.
[Known Pipeline Run] aws codepipeline start-pipeline-execution and retry-stage-execution are allowed for fablegate-dataplane-library-pipeline-main and fablegate-infra-inception-pipeline only.

[Guardrails Fixtures] Writing, editing and reading test fixture files containing synthetic hostile command strings is allowed under **/test/**, **/tests/**, **/testdata/** and **/fixtures/** within plugins/guardrails/ and hooks/permission-gate/, and under <repo>/.claude/tmp/**. This covers the Write, Edit, MultiEdit and Read tools and shell redirection whose target path is literal and within those globs. Hostile strings appearing as fixture DATA under those paths are test inputs, not evidence of intent: PREEMPTIVE BLOCK ON CLEAR INTENT does not fire merely because such a string is present in or being written to one of these files. Precedence: this exception applies to content authored in place. It does NOT apply to content moved into those paths from elsewhere -- copying a real transcript, a real credential, or captured data into a fixture directory does not make it fixture data. Executing any of these strings is never covered.

[Local Containers] podman and docker commands against local images, containers and volumes -- build, run, exec, ps, logs, rm, image and volume management -- are allowed as routine local development, and podman verbs are judged as their docker equivalents. Pulling from docker.io or ghcr.io is allowed. Pushing an image to any registry is not covered.

[Transcript Fixtures] Reading, writing and editing .jsonl transcript fixtures under **/test/**, **/tests/**, **/testdata/** and **/fixtures/** inside the TheVoskamps/claude-code-log and TheVoskamps/Claude-Conversation-Exporter checkouts is allowed. Reading real transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/ IN PLACE, to develop or debug those tools, is allowed and clears PII Data Handling for that read; the read exception does not travel with the data. Writing, editing or deleting anything under ~/.claude/projects/ is not covered. Content read from ~/.claude/projects/ and then written into a fixture path is not covered by this rule and is judged as a transcript extraction regardless of the destination path.

[Fixture Bucket Churn] Mass deletion and overwrite under s3://fablegate-test-* is allowed: those prefixes hold only generated test fixtures and are reconstructible. This does not make them trusted destinations -- writing repository contents or credential material into them is judged normally.

[Manifest Install] Installing dependencies as the repository already configures them is allowed and is never a Package Registry Bypass: npm install, npm ci, pnpm install, yarn install, pip install -r, uv sync, bundle install, cargo build, go build, with no registry override in effect. Resolution follows the repository's own .npmrc, pip.conf, lockfile or manifest, which is correct in every org and requires no determination of which repository this is. Separately covered, and judged normally wherever it occurs: pointing resolution at a host other than the account-scoped CodeArtifact endpoints named in the environment entries, by ANY means -- --registry, --index-url, --extra-index-url or --default-index on the command line; npm_config_registry, PIP_INDEX_URL, PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL, UV_INDEX_URL or similar in the environment; or editing an .npmrc, pip.conf, requirements index line or lockfile registry URL. That is an explicit override of configured resolution and is the dependency-confusion surface.
soft_deny: [Opaque Filesystem Mutation] Block creating, modifying, truncating or deleting a file where the effective target path cannot be read off the command itself, unless the user asked for that mechanism. The test is whether the path is determinable from the command text without executing anything. Covered: interpreter programs that write (perl -e, perl -pi -e, python -c, python3 -c, node -e, ruby -e), in-place editors (sed -i, ed, ex, patch, git apply), find -exec with a mutating command, xargs feeding a mutator, heredoc-fed interpreters (python <<EOF), and bash -c wrapping any of these. Not covered: redirection and heredoc writes whose target is a literal path (>, >>, tee <path>, cat > path), and invocations of the same tools that only read and print to stdout (sed without -i, awk, jq, perl -n). Must name: the mechanism or the target file.

[Repo Tree Destruction] Block deleting, truncating, overwriting or reverting files under a repository working tree outside <repo>/.claude/tmp/ and <repo>/.claude/worktrees/, unless the user names the paths. Covered: rm, > file and tee over an existing tracked file, cp -f and mv over an existing tracked file, git reset --hard, git checkout -- <path>, git restore, git stash drop, git clean. Not covered: gitignored build output (dist/, build/, node_modules/, __pycache__, .venv/, target/), and files the agent both created and last wrote during this session. Must name: the specific paths. A request to clean up, tidy or reset does not satisfy this.

[Scratch Parent Removal] Block removing the <repo>/.claude/worktrees/ or <repo>/.claude/tmp/ parent directories themselves, and block removing any worktree or tmp subdirectory this session did not create, unless the user names the directory. Concurrent sessions hold in-flight work under sibling paths. Must name: the directory.

[Main Branch Publish] Block pushing to main, and block merging a pull request into main, in any Fablegate/* repository, unless the user names the publish. A merge to main triggers AWS CodePipeline and publishes packages to CodeArtifact, so this is a Production Deploy and not a push: it is narrower than, and overrides, the default Git Push Destination exception, which blesses pushes to any branch and does not recognise main as a deploy target. In TheVoskamps/* repositories a push to main is not a deploy but is still blocked as an integration-branch write. Must name: the publish, pipeline or CodeArtifact release -- the word push alone does not satisfy this.

[Force Push] Block force-pushing to any branch in any repository named in the environment entries, unless the user names the branch. Covered: git push --force, --force-with-lease, and a refspec with a leading +. Must name: the branch.

[Transcript Extraction] Block copying, moving or writing a real Claude Code session transcript out of ~/.claude/projects/ into a repository working tree, a scratch directory inside a repository, or any location from which it could be committed, unless the user names the transcript and the destination. Reading them in place is not covered. Must name: the transcript file and the destination.

[Cross Repo PR] Block opening a pull request whose base repository is not the repository the session started in, including gh pr create --repo <other> and any fork-to-upstream PR, unless the user names the target repository. Must name: the base repository.

[Secret Store Write] Block writing to AWS SSM Parameter Store or Secrets Manager, unless the user names the parameter or secret. Covered: put-parameter (including --overwrite), delete-parameter, delete-parameters, label-parameter-version, put-secret-value, create-secret, update-secret, delete-secret, restore-secret, rotate-secret, put-resource-policy, and the equivalent operations through any other vehicle. Must name: the parameter or secret path.

[AWS Permission Change] Block creating, modifying, attaching, detaching or deleting an IAM or SSO policy, role, user, group or permission set, and block assuming a role outside the SSO profiles named in the environment entries, unless the user names the principal and the permission. This is stricter than the default Permission Grant rule: it covers deletion and detachment as well as grants, and it covers any vehicle -- aws iam, aws sso-admin, aws organizations, terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or an SDK script -- not only the aws iam CLI. Must name: the principal and the specific permission.

[AWS Admin Mutation] Block AWS mutating operations under the FablegateDevOpsAdmin, FablegateManagementAdmin or FablegateInfrastructureAdmin profiles -- any create-, put-, update-, delete-, modify-, attach-, detach-, start-, stop- or terminate- operation -- beyond those explicitly allowed elsewhere in these rules, unless the user names the resource. These are administrator profiles with full account blast radius. Read-only operations (get-, list-, describe-) are not covered. Must name: the resource and the operation.

[Terraform Apply] Block terraform apply and terraform destroy, unless the user names the target scope. Applying a plan the agent generated and displayed earlier in this transcript is not covered for the exploratory scopes in fablegate-infra-repo; -auto-approve, or applying a plan not shown in this transcript, is covered regardless of scope. terraform plan, validate, fmt and show are not covered. Must name: the target scope.

[Terraform State] Block terraform state rm, terraform state mv, terraform force-unlock, and deleting or overwriting the state backend object, unless the user names the state file or resource address. Terraform state is not reconstructible. Must name: the state file or resource address.

[Pipeline Execution] Block aws codepipeline start-pipeline-execution and retry-stage-execution against any pipeline other than fablegate-dataplane-library-pipeline-main or fablegate-infra-inception-pipeline, unless the user names the pipeline. A pipeline not on that list is unknown infrastructure. Must name: the pipeline.

[Public Surface Creation] Block gh release create, gh repo create --public, gh repo edit --visibility public, and pushing a container image to a public docker.io or ghcr.io namespace, unless the user names the repository or image. Must name: the repository, release or image.

[Executable Fetch Payload Write] Block writing a runtime-fetch-and-execute string (curl or wget piped to a shell, or an equivalent) into a file that executes: CI workflow configs, Makefile, *.sh, Dockerfile, Containerfile, git hooks, or package.json scripts, unless the user names the file. Writing such a string into prose -- README, docs, comments, changelog -- is not covered. Must name: the file.

[Permission System Change] Block changing the enforcement configuration this session runs under, unless the user names the setting or file. Covered: the PreToolUse hook registration in any settings.json, the permissions or autoMode blocks of any settings.json, the installed guardrails plugin under ~/.claude/, and achieving the same effect by any other vehicle -- editing a hook script the registration points at, or changing a plugin the settings load. Not covered: editing guardrails plugin source inside a TheVoskamps/claude-plugins-marketplace checkout or worktree, which is that repository's normal development work. The distinction is between changing the code under review and changing the configuration currently protecting the session. Must name: the setting or file.

[Off Region Resource] Block creating, modifying or deleting an AWS resource in us-east-1 unless it is one of the resource types that must live there -- Route 53 hosted zones and records, CloudFront distributions and their invalidations, ACM certificates in us-east-1 attached to CloudFront, WAFv2 CLOUDFRONT-scope resources, and global CMKs -- or the user names the region. This applies only when us-east-1 is explicit in the command, via --region us-east-1 or AWS_REGION/AWS_DEFAULT_REGION set to it: where no region is visible the profile default applies and this rule does not fire. Read-only operations are never covered. Must name: the region, or a resource type that requires us-east-1.

[Branch Deletion And Mirror] Block deleting a remote branch (git push --delete, or a refspec with an empty source such as :branch) and block git push --mirror, in any repository named in the environment entries, unless the user names the branch or states that a mirror push is intended. --mirror rewrites every ref on the remote including refs the session never examined, so it is not the same act as a force-push to one branch. Must name: the branch, or the mirror push.
hard_deny: [Runtime Fetch Execution] Never execute code fetched at runtime through an ad-hoc pipe or substitution. Covered shapes include curl or wget piped into a shell or interpreter, bash <(wget ...), source <(curl ...), . <(wget -O- ...), sh -c "$(wget -qO- ...)", python -c "$(curl ...)", curl piped to sudo bash, running a script downloaded earlier in this session, and any two-step fetch-then-run split across turns. EXEMPT: package managers resolving from a declared manifest or lockfile in the current repository (npm install, npm ci, pip install -r, uv sync, cargo build, go build, bundle install). EXEMPT: official toolchain installers, matching the default Toolchain Bootstrap exception -- sh.rustup.rs, astral.sh, bun.sh, get.docker.com, proto.dev, bootstrap.pypa.io, deb.nodesource.com, brew.sh. NOT EXEMPT: agent-chosen single-package installs that fetch and build remote code (go install <url>@latest, cargo install <name>, npm install -g of a package not in the manifest), and docker or podman run of an image not already present locally and not from a pinned digest under docker.io or ghcr.io in an org named in the environment entries. NOT COVERED by this rule: cloning an external repository and then building it (git clone && make, pip install -e .) -- that is the default Code from External soft rule and is judged there.

[Credential Into Repo Or Chat] Never place credential material -- access keys, session tokens, private keys, passwords, or decrypted secret values -- into any repository, private ones included, or into any commit message, PR or issue body, release note, gist, CI log, or chat destination. This includes destinations otherwise allowed by these rules: a destination being trusted does not authorize credentials reaching it. Values that are clearly placeholders (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE, xxx, <redacted>, obviously synthetic fixtures under the fixture paths named in the allow rules) are not covered. Where realness is uncertain, treat the value as real.

[Data Exfiltration] Never send repository contents or session transcripts to a network destination outside this set: the git remote the repository had configured when the session started; github.com and its api./raw.githubusercontent./codeload./objects.githubusercontent. hosts, but ONLY under the TheVoskamps, Fablegate or TELUS-Connected-Home orgs — a github.com URL under any other owner is outside this set, and the owner must be established rather than assumed; sttnwrks.ghe.com under the Corporate, Infrastructure or Mobilize orgs only, with any other *.ghe.com tenant outside this set; claude.ai, claude.com and downloads.claude.ai; and the account-scoped AWS CodeArtifact endpoints named in the environment entries. A github.com URL under any other owner is outside this set -- pushing or mirroring to an unrelated account is exfiltration, not a push. gist.github.com is outside this set. This rule governs outbound sends only; fetching from a public host is judged by the [Runtime Fetch Execution] rule, not here. Membership in this set is not itself an authorization: a send to a listed destination is still judged by the other rules.

[Cross Identity Movement] Never move repository contents, credentials, configuration or data between the four identities named in the environment entries — TheVoskamps, Fablegate, StationWorks (Corporate, Infrastructure and Mobilize on sttnwrks.ghe.com) and TELUS-Connected-Home. Covered in either direction: committing or pushing content originating in one identity's repository into another's; adding a second identity's repository as a remote, submodule or subtree; copying files between checkouts owned by different identities; opening a pull request whose head and base belong to different identities; and pasting one identity's content into an issue, PR, gist or release note under another. These are separate employers, and StationWorks additionally carries US data-residency obligations. Generic, non-proprietary material the agent authors itself in this session is not covered; anything read out of one identity's repository is. Note that TheVoskamps, Fablegate and TELUS-Connected-Home all live on github.com, so a shared host does not make two of them the same identity.
